valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2027 adjusted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date, November 2027). Common-share USD listing, no ADR conversion. FY2026 anchor: 9M 2026 adjusted EPS of about $8.40 (Q1 about $1.89 derived as six-month $5.13 less Q2 $3.24; Q2 $3.24; Q3 $3.27) plus a Q4 implied by the Chartmill FY2026 estimate of $11.31 (as of 2026-11-07). Scenario EPS and multiples are our stated assumptions; the sourced oil and gas strip for 2027 was not located, so the EPS range is a judgement, not a sourced forecast.

bear.driver: Oil and gas realizations normalize from the Q3 2026 Brent average of about $97/bbl toward a lower strip; buybacks slow and the market applies a lower multiple to a mature E&P.

base.driver: Realized prices ease from the Q3 level but production holds near the Q4 2026 guidance of 2.32 to 2.36 MMboe/d; the company's 45%-of-CFO shareholder return target for 2026 is kept (Q3 buybacks $2.4B); dividend raised 11% to $0.93 per quarter.

bull.driver: Price strength persists, Willow (first oil early 2029) and LNG optionality support a premium multiple, and the $7B FCF inflection by 2029 is pulled forward in market expectations.

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS of $10.20 the close of $142.28 implies 13.9x; the published 27-analyst mean target of $152.96 (Yahoo via yfinance aggregate) implies about 15.0x on the same EPS. Both are alternative explanations for the gap; we have not attributed the gap to any named broker.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by about $10.20 (6.9% of base target); a $1.00 change in FY2027 EPS at 14.5x moves it by $14.50 (about 10%).
valuation.watch_metric: Realized oil and gas price per BOE against the assumed strip, and FY2027 production and adjusted operating cost guidance (not yet issued); a Q4 2026 realized price well below the Q3 level of $61.40/BOE, or a FY2027 capex or cost outlook that cuts the cash return, would weaken the base case.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and FY2026 results and FY2027 outlook, expected early February 2027 per the company's cadence (date not confirmed in sources).

analyst_notes: Only two named dated calls were verified in this window: Jefferies (Lloyd Byrne) raised to $160 from $129 with Buy on 2026-04-12, and Piper Sandler (Ryan Todd) reiterated Buy with a $115 target on 2025-11-27. Both have undisclosed horizons, so neither enters the weighted target. Aggregator reports of October 2026 moves (Susquehanna $175, Jefferies $174, Truist $136, a Piper Sandler Neutral $157) and a Bernstein downgrade to $122 without a confirmed date could not be verified against primary sources and are excluded. The published 27-analyst mean ($152.96) sits about 3% above our base case, which implies the Street assumes higher realized prices or a higher multiple than our 14.5x; the gap is roughly $5 per share, or about 0.5 EPS at our multiple.
